annotation.title_clean: Experimental and Integrative Approaches to Robo-ethics. An Introduction
annotation.title_en: Experimental and Integrative Approaches to Robo-ethics. An Introduction
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bianchini, F.; Damiano, L.; Datteri, E.; Graziani, P.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Editorial introduction to a special issue of the International Journal of Social Robotics on experimental and integrative robo-ethics. It summarises articles on the Collingridge dilemma, perceived safety, cobot democratization, roboticists' views on the EU civil law rules on robotics, artificial emotions, assistive robots in education, and persuasive robots.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robo-ethics needs experimental and integrative methods alongside philosophical analysis.
Interdisciplinary collaboration is essential for ethical regulation of robotics.
Perceived safety adds psychological and social dimensions to physical safety in HRI.
Inclusive, responsibility-oriented design addresses the Collingridge dilemma in social robotics.
Roboticists were surveyed on the EU Draft Report on Civil Law Rules on Robotics.
